title: Duality along a finite flat morphism of smooth curves
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $C$ a smooth
connected curve over $k$, $f:C\to\mathbf P^1_k$
a finite flat morphism of smooth $k$-curves, and $\mathcal M$ a
finite locally free $\mathcal O_C$-module (a quasi-coherent module which
is Zariski-locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_C^{\oplus r}$ for some
$r\ge0$), with dual
$\mathcal M^{\vee}:=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_C}(\mathcal M,\mathcal O_C)$.
Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}\bigl(f_*\mathcal M,\;
\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\bigr)\;\cong\;
H^0\bigl(C,\;\omega_C\otimes\mathcal M^{\vee}\bigr);
$$

in particular, for an invertible $\mathcal M$
([def-sc-invertible-module]) the right hand side is
$H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal M^{-1})$. Here $\omega_{\mathbf P^1}:=\Omega^1_{\mathbf P^1_k/k}$ and
$\omega_C:=\Omega^1_{C/k}$
([def-sc-kahler-differentials]).
(*Source: the classical Grothendieck duality for finite
morphisms – the trace/fundamental-class isomorphism
$\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}(f_*\mathcal O_C, \omega_{\mathbf P^1})\cong f_*\omega_C$ attached to a finite flat
morphism, i.e. Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, III, (6.10),
(6.12); the local algebra is the classical computation of the
different/codifferent of a finite flat extension of discrete
valuation rings, Serre, *Local Fields*, Ch. II, $\S$4.*)

proof.text: For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset\mathbf P^1_k$, finiteness makes $f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ affine. For the $B$-module $M$ representing $\mathcal M$ and the $R$-module $N$ representing a target sheaf, restriction of scalars has the explicit adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,\operatorname{Hom}_R(B,N))$, carrying $\phi$ to $m\mapsto(b\mapsto\phi(bm))$. These maps commute with localization, so they give the corresponding sheaf adjunction.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: affine restriction-of-scalars adjunction

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-finite-duality-trace] to the finite flat $k$-morphism $f$ from the smooth curve $C$. Its comparison map gives the canonical sheaf isomorphism $f_*\omega_C\cong\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}(f_*\mathcal O_C,\omega_{\mathbf P^1})$. The theorem includes the ramified local calculation; no choice of uniformizers or tame-ramification formula is needed here.

Use the affine adjunction of step one with $\mathcal F=\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal G=\omega_{\mathbf P^1}$, then the trace comparison of step two. The trace comparison $\omega\mapsto(a\mapsto\tau(a\omega))$ is $f_*\mathcal O_C$-linear, so it passes through the adjunction from step one. Equivalently, on affine opens the $B$-linear map $M\to\Omega^1_{B/k}$ is sent to the $R$-linear map $M\to\Omega^1_{R/k}$ by composing with the trace, yielding $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}(f_*\mathcal M,\omega_{\mathbf P^1})\cong H^0(C,\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_C}(\mathcal M,\omega_C))$. Since $\mathcal M$ is finite locally free, $\omega_C\otimes\mathcal M^{\vee}\to\mathcal H om(\mathcal M,\omega_C)$ is an isomorphism: on each open where $\mathcal M\cong\mathcal O_C^{\oplus r}$ it is the identity on $r$ copies of $\omega_C$, including $r=0$. Taking global sections proves the displayed isomorphism. For invertible $\mathcal M$, [lem-sc-invertible-dual] identifies $\mathcal M^{\vee}$ with $\mathcal M^{-1}$.
